lead.label: 5j
lead.why: Abstract: 'compound 5j (IC50 = 2.78 uM), bearing ethoxy at the 4-position of the phenyl ring, was found to be the most active compound in this series'; also the compound used for tubulin polymerisation, cell-cycle, apoptosis and docking studies.

reactions.conditions: Friedel-Crafts acylation: 1 (12 mmol), phenylacetic acid 2 (8 mmol), TFAA (16 mmol), TFA (5 mL), rt, overnight (12 h in scheme); pour into water, extract EtOAc, chromatography
reactions.source: Sec. 2.1, Sec. 4.1.1 (general procedure for 3), Scheme 1 step a

reactions.conditions: 3 (5 mmol) in DMF-DMA (12 mL), 80 C, 24 h; concentrate, silica gel chromatography
reactions.source: Sec. 4.1.2 (general procedure for 4), Scheme 1 step b

reactions.conditions: 4 (0.5 mmol), N2H4.H2O (3 equiv), isopropanol, rt 1 h then 40 C 1 h; pour into water, extract EtOAc, silica gel chromatography (PE/EtOAc); 56%
reactions.source: Sec. 4.1.3 (general procedure for 5a-5q), Sec. 4.1.13 (5j), Scheme 1 step c

notes: The enamine 4j and deoxybenzoin 3j are made in situ in the general procedures but their individual names are not printed (name ''); structures derived from the text (Friedel-Crafts at C4 of 1-methoxynaphthalene, consistent with the 4-methoxynaphthalen-1-yl group in 5j). The enamine alkene geometry is unspecified. The 4-ethoxyphenylacetic acid is identified from the product's 4-ethoxyphenyl group; the paper says only 'appropriate commercially available phenylacetic acids'. The pyrazole N-H tautomer is drawn as in the printed name (1H, 4-aryl, 5-naphthyl). Text says reaction (a) is overnight; scheme says 12 h.
